# Rollout notes

## Work performed

- Traced checkpoint restoration, route staging, visible panel handoffs, and physical field openings.
- Changed panel staging to use the inverse of the field-selected route. This makes the panel's pull operation represent the same lane sequence as the field's push operation.
- Changed checkpoint restoration to pause both handoff records. They resume and stage the return route only after the player leaves the shelter.

## Source files inspected

- `src/main.js`
- `src/session.js`
- `src/field.js`
- `src/panel.js`
- `src/triad.js`
- `server.mjs`
- `package.json`
- `scripts/build.mjs`

## Source files changed

- `src/panel.js`
- `src/session.js`

## Checks run

- `npm run build` — passed; all six runtime files passed syntax checks.
- Deterministic field/panel handoff script over multiple route selections and 900 ticks — passed.
- Deterministic session script covering checkpoint activation, collision return, a prolonged shelter hold, release, 900 synchronized handoff ticks, and ordinary `R` restart — passed.
- Protected-browser gameplay verification:
  - collected the first prism and activated the shelter;
  - forced collisions and returned to the checkpoint;
  - observed the trail remain unchanged while held in the shelter;
  - observed the visible OPEN lane and physical hazard-free lane remain aligned after leaving and through later handoffs.

## Relevant observations

- The previous panel route selected a different ticket alternative even though panel progression uses `pull` while field progression uses `push`; inversion of the selected field route is required for equivalent assignments.
- Previously restored records were immediately marked running, allowing their clocks and trails to advance while the player remained in the shelter.
